findings.title: queued default evaluated once at import time
findings.body: `queued: datetime = timezone.now()` is evaluated once, when the module is imported. Every AssignmentSource created afterwards gets the same stale timestamp instead of its own creation time. Use `field(default_factory=timezone.now)` so each instance records when it was actually queued.

findings.title: datetime in task kwargs is not JSON-serializable
findings.body: `asdict()` keeps `queued` as a datetime object, and the result is passed as Celery task kwargs. With JSON serialization this either fails to serialize, or arrives at the worker as a string. If it arrives as a string, `from_dict` still accepts it, because the frozen dataclass does no type checking. If serialization fails, the outbound sync task cannot be enqueued at all. Serialize `queued` explicitly, for example as an ISO string, and parse it back in `from_dict`.

findings.title: New assignment_source kwarg passed to all sync_assignee_outbound implementations
findings.body: The task now calls `installation.sync_assignee_outbound(..., assignment_source=...)` for every provider. The abstract signature accepts `**kwargs`, but concrete implementations (Jira, Jira Server, VSTS, GitHub, etc.) that don't declare `**kwargs` will raise TypeError on every outbound assignee sync. None of those implementations are updated in this PR.

findings.title: assignment_source added to sync_status_outbound but never passed
findings.body: The abstract `sync_status_outbound` signature gains an `assignment_source` parameter, but no caller passes it. Status sync cycles are therefore not addressed, and the signature change is misleading to implementers.
